domain_setting: A calm shared office with workstations, paper records, desktop technology, and everyday writing supplies.
visual_thesis: Make each object immediately recognizable in an office task, using blank paper, abstract screen marks, and simple gestures instead of readable words or numbers.
global_art_direction: Ground tools and equipment in a clean office desk, workstation, file area, or paper-handling task; vary the scene while preserving a shared visual language.

Keep confusing neighboring concepts visually distinct: desktop monitor versus whole computer, copier versus printer versus scanner, paper file versus computer file, pen versus pencil, stapler versus staples, folder versus envelope.
Use blank sheets and geometric marks only; screens, calendars, planners, spreadsheets, and notes must contain no readable letters or numerals.
Use five labeled structural SVG layers, a 0 0 304 192 viewBox, Artico palette variables, clear silhouettes, and no text or tspan elements.
Objects should occupy the center of the card and retain enough size and contrast to read in a small vocabulary tile.

same_term_course_art_reviewed.reason: A single backrest chair is clear and semantically correct; the basic term does not require a swivel mechanism.
A writing desk with a drawer and open book reads clearly as a work table and fits the office context.
The standing lamp is a clear generic lamp; it remains plausible office lighting.
The waste container and discarded paper are immediately clear; the household pedal detail does not change the object sense.
A wall adapter and connected phone show the same device-charging sense used in an office.
The all-in-one computer is a clear office computer and avoids confusing it with the separate desktop-computer entry.
The computer keycaps, space bar, and cord clearly identify a computer keyboard rather than piano keys.
The open portable computer is a clear laptop suitable for the office setting.
The sculpted pointer with scroll wheel and cable is the computer accessory required by this group.
The animal image is the wrong sense for an office-computing group; use the reviewed computer mouse from Lesson 76.
A locked access symbol communicates a password-protected account without relying on lettering.
The prior card is a ridged hand tool; this chapter uses a paper office file, so new file-folder art is required.
The paper letter and envelope depict written correspondence, which fits office files and planning.
The pivot and two loop handles clearly show scissors; the physical tool is the same in kitchen and office use.

reviewed_existing_art.reason: Twelve clear same-term office-compatible illustrations will be reused. The animal mouse and workshop file are rejected as wrong senses; all other terms have no exact same-term art candidate and will be authored for the office chapter.

entries.chair: A sturdy office chair with a back, padded seat, armrests, central height-adjustment post, and small casters.
entries.desk: A broad office work table with a writing surface, modest drawer, and papers arranged for desk work.
entries.drawer: One desk drawer pulled open far enough to reveal its box interior and paper supplies.
entries.filing cabinet: A tall metal office cabinet with stacked file drawers, recessed pulls, and tabbed folders visible in one open drawer.
entries.lamp: Reuse the clear generic standing lamp from Lesson 9; it remains plausible office lighting.
entries.office equipment: A compact grouping of office devices such as a monitor, telephone, copier, and desk lamp arranged around a workstation.
entries.trays: Two or three stacked in-trays holding neatly separated blank sheets and folders.
entries.trash can / bin (uk, for a trash can): An office waste basket beside the desk with a few crumpled paper balls visible.
entries.cell phone: A mobile phone standing on the desk beside a small charging cable, clearly portable and handheld.
entries.charger: Reuse the clear wall adapter and charging phone from Lesson 76.
entries.computer: Reuse the clear all-in-one computer from Lesson 76; it is a general office computer, distinct from the laptop.
entries.copier / photocopier: A large office copier with a document on the glass, lid, control panel, paper tray, and duplicate sheets emerging.
entries.headset: An office-call headset with two padded earcups, a headband, and a small boom microphone near the mouth.
entries.keyboard: Reuse the clear computer keyboard with square keycaps and a space bar from Lesson 76.
entries.laptop: Reuse the clear open portable laptop from Lesson 76.
entries.monitor: A separate computer display on a stand with a thin screen and simple abstract window blocks; do not add a computer tower.
entries.mouse: Reuse the clear sculpted computer mouse with scroll wheel and cable from Lesson 76, not the animal from Lesson 54.
entries.password: Reuse the clear locked account symbol from Lesson 76; keep it free of letters and numerals.
entries.phone / telephone: A landline desk telephone with a handset, coiled cord, keypad buttons without numerals, and a small base.
entries.printer: A compact office printer feeds one blank page out of a paper slot, distinct from the larger copier.
entries.projector: A small presentation projector casts a bright geometric image toward a blank wall or pull-down screen.
entries.scanner: A flatbed office scanner with a raised lid and a visible scanning bar moving beneath a sheet of paper.
entries.shredder: A desktop paper shredder draws a sheet into its slot and releases narrow paper strips into a bin.
entries.spreadsheet: A monitor shows an orderly grid of colored cells and a simple chart without letters, labels, or numbers.
entries.bulletin board / notice board (also used: A wall-mounted pinboard holds a few blank notices, a small calendar sheet, and colored pushpins.
entries.calendar: A standing or wall calendar uses a clean grid with one highlighted square, no readable dates or numbers.
entries.clipboard: A rigid board holds one blank paper sheet under a strong top clip, ready for note-taking.
entries.diary: An open personal diary with a ribbon marker and blank ruled pages, shown as a bound book.
entries.envelope: A single paper envelope with a triangular flap and sealed seam, clearly separate from the letter sheet.
entries.file / files: A paper file folder with a projecting tab holds several organized blank documents; no hand tool or computer window.
entries.folder / folders: A closed tabbed document folder beside a second folder, showing the covers and labeled tabs without writing.
entries.letter: Reuse the clear paper correspondence scene from Lesson 7; the chapter meaning is a written message, not an alphabet character.
entries.notepad: A small top-bound pad with a stack of blank sheets and a short pencil beside it.
entries.planner: An open weekly planner with a simple block layout, check marks, and pen; no readable words or dates.
entries.sticky notes: Several small square adhesive notes in a fan or on the edge of a board, each a different solid color and blank.
entries.adhesive tape: A clear tape roll with its end peeled away and a short strip fixed to a blank sheet.
entries.binder clip: A black triangular spring clip grips a neat stack of paper, with its two wire handles standing out.
entries.correction fluid: A small correction-fluid bottle with brush applicator covers one dark abstract mark on a blank page.
entries.thumbtack / drawing pin (mainly uk): A flat-headed pushpin is pressed through a blank note into a cork notice board.
entries.eraser / rubber (uk, for an eraser): A small block eraser rubs away a graphite line beside a pencil on paper.
entries.highlighter: A broad chisel-tip marker lays a translucent yellow stripe across blank paper without highlighting words.
entries.hole punch: A desktop punch presses through paper while two neat circular chads fall into its tray.
entries.paper clips: Several bent wire clips hold the corners of loose office sheets together.
entries.pen: A capped ballpoint pen with pocket clip and fine writing tip rests beside a short blue ink line.
entries.pencil: A sharpened yellow graphite pencil with a visible wooden point, dark lead, and eraser cap.
entries.pencil sharpener: A compact hand sharpener grips a pencil point while fresh curled shavings collect beside it.
entries.rubber band: A stretched elastic band wraps around a neat stack of office papers, with one loose loop visible.
entries.ruler: A straight transparent ruler lies along a measured line; show evenly spaced ticks but no numerals.
entries.scissors: Reuse the clear two-blade scissors with central pivot and loops from Lesson 10.
entries.stapler: A desktop stapler is pressed down over two paper sheets, fastening their corner with one staple.
entries.staples: A short strip of small silver U-shaped staples beside two sheets joined at one corner; do not show the stapler as the main object.
entries.stationery: A tidy collection of pen, pencil, ruler, eraser, paper clips, and notepad arranged in an office supply tray.
